- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model may lag; forecast should align with recent low if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; dampen forecast volatility if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model tends to “average out” — don’t follow this; instead, weight recent sentiment more heavily (last 5–7 days).
- When true outcome is consistently higher than forecast (e.g., +1.5–2.5% over 30d), model underestimates long-term trend — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per week if sentiment is bullish.
- If forecast is consistently lower than true outcome, model may be missing sentiment-driven momentum — check if sentiment is trending up and adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.7% per day if sentiment > 0.67.
